name: Deep teal green
lede: Deep teal green is a dark, blue-leaning green, a shade down from plain [[teal]].

sections.title: Two readings of one hex
sections.body:
The ISCC-NBS system of 1955 classes the swatch as moderate bluish green, about 2.9 units from its block center, and Ridgway's 1912 nomenclature carries the same hex without a matching plate reading [1]. Our library lists the identical hex again under [[deep-teal-green]], a separate ISCC-NBS and Ridgway reading at zero distance, so two names here point to one screen color [1][2].

The closest distinct color is [[myrtle-green]], about 3.4 units away, with [[dark-aquamarine]] and [[dark-green-blue]] further out [2]. The name itself simply marks a deep step on the [[deep-teal]] ladder [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: This color, as photographed, appears in 40 of 23,781 paintings, rarer than 62 percent of the named colors we track [3]. It peaks in the 1900s, in 9 of 1,674 paintings, at 0.5 per cent of that century's paintings, 4.6 times the overall rate [3]. Inside a painting it most often plays a hidden color, tucked into shadow rather than carrying the light [3]. The earliest match in the archive is a 1490 painting by the Master of the Saint John Panels, well before the name's 1912 record, so the match is a look-alike hue in an aged photograph, not a pigment test, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [3].
